### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide *(No special software needed; just your hands, patience, and a bit of elbow grease.)* --- #### 1️⃣ Plan & Budget | Category | Typical Cost Range | Notes | |----------|-------------------|-------| | **CPU** | $100–$600+ | Pick an Intel Core i5/i7/AMD Ryzen 5/7 depending on workload. | | **Motherboard** | $80–$300 | Match socket (e.g., LGA 1700, AM4) + features you care about (Wi‑Fi, RGB). | | **RAM** | $40–$200 | DDR4 vs DDR5; 16GB is safe for most users, 32GB for gaming/multitasking. | | **GPU** | $150–$1200+ | Depends on gaming needs; integrated graphics if budget tight. | | **Storage** | $50–$250 | NVMe SSDs (~500GB+) offer fastest boot times. Add HDD later if more space needed. | | **Power Supply Unit (PSU)** | $60–$180 | Get ≥80 Plus Bronze rating; calculate wattage using online PSU calculators. | | **Case** | $30–$200 | Size matters—ATX, Micro‑ATX, Mini‑ITX. Consider airflow, cable management. | | **Cooling** | $20–$150 | Stock cooler often enough; aftermarket air coolers ($30–70) or AIO liquid coolers ($90–140). | | **Operating System** | Free (Linux) / ~$15 (Windows Home) | Windows license key required unless you use free alternatives. | > **Tip:** Use sites like *PCPartPicker* to check component compatibility and price alerts before purchasing. --- #### 2️⃣ Gather Your Toolkit | Tool | Why It Helps | |------|--------------| | Phillips #2 screwdriver | Most screws on boards/cases. | | Anti‑static wrist strap | Prevent static discharge damaging components. | | Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied) | Improves heat transfer between CPU & cooler. | | Cable ties / Velcro straps | Keep cables tidy inside the case. | | Small flathead screwdriver or pry tool | For opening panels without scratching. | | Flashlight or headlamp | Good lighting improves visibility. | --- #### 3️⃣ Safety First 1. **Work on a non‑conductive surface** (wood table, plastic mat). 2. **Ground yourself**: wear an anti‑static band or touch a grounded metal object frequently. 3. **Turn off all peripherals**, unplug from mains, remove battery if laptop style. 4. **Keep track of screws**: label them or keep separate piles per part. --- #### 4️⃣ Assemble Inside the Case ##### 4.1 Prepare the Motherboard 1. **Install I/O shield** into the back panel of the case first. 2. Place the motherboard onto the standoffs (pre‑installed in many cases). - Align screw holes with standoff slots. 3. Secure it lightly with screws (do NOT overtighten). ##### 4.2 Install Power Supply 1. Mount PSU in its compartment (usually bottom rear). 2. Connect the main 24‑pin ATX connector to the motherboard. 3. Attach the 8‑pin EPS (or 4‑pin) CPU power plug near the CPU socket. 4. Route other connectors (SATA, PCIe) toward where they’ll connect later. ##### 4.3 Insert Storage Drives - **NVMe M.2 SSD**: Slide into the dedicated slot on the motherboard, secure with one small screw. - **HDD/SSD SATA drives**: Put into drive bays, attach data and power cables. ##### 4.4 Install the CPU 1. Lift the CPU socket lever. 2. Line up the corner triangle on the CPU with the matching mark on the socket. 3. Gently place the CPU down (no force). 4. Lower the lever to lock it in place. ##### 4.5 Apply Thermal Paste & Cooler - If cooler has pre‑applied paste, skip this step. - Otherwise apply pea‑size amount of thermal paste on top center of CPU. - Mount the cooler according to manufacturer’s instructions (attach brackets, then mount to socket). - Tighten evenly to avoid uneven pressure. ##### 4.6 Install Memory (RAM) 1. Open DIMM slots’ clips. 2. Align notch on stick with slot gap. 3. Push firmly until clicks both sides. Repeat for second module if dual‑channel desired. ##### 4.7 Mount Graphics Card (If Using One) 1. Remove appropriate expansion slot covers from the case front. 2. Insert card into the topmost PCIe x16 slot. 3. Firmly press until it locks. 4. Screw the bracket to the case. 5. Connect required PCIe power cables from PSU. ##### 4.8 Wire Everything Together - **Data Cables**: SATA data lines from storage to motherboard. - **Power Cables**: SATA power to drives, optional additional fans. - **Front Panel Connectors**: USB ports, audio jacks, power button, reset switch – refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. - **Fans**: Connect chassis fan headers; set speed via BIOS or software later. ##### 4.9 Final Checks Before Closing - Verify no loose screws or wires obstruct fans. - Ensure all connections are snug. - Double‑check orientation of GPU and PSU cables. --- #### 5️⃣ Close Up & Initial Boot 1. Replace side panels. 2. Reconnect monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers. 3. Plug in power cord, turn on PSU toggle. 4. Press computer's power button. On first boot: - Enter BIOS/UEFI (`Del`, `F2`, etc.). - Check that CPU, memory, storage appear correctly. - Set correct boot order (USB/DVD → Hard Drive). - Save changes and exit. --- #### 6️⃣ Install Operating System | Option | Steps | |--------|-------| | **Windows 10/11** | • Create bootable USB with Media Creation Tool.
• Select custom install during setup.
• Format target partition (NTFS).
• Follow prompts. | | **Ubuntu Linux** | • Download ISO, create live USB with Rufus.
• Boot from USB, choose “Try Ubuntu” or “Install”.
• Partition as desired (ext4 recommended). | | **Other distros** | Similar procedure; consult distro docs. | After installation: - Update drivers (especially GPU). - Run system updates. - Configure backup solution. --- #### 7️⃣ Post‑Build Tweaks & Maintenance | Task | Frequency | How | |------|-----------|-----| | Clean dust | Every 3 months | Use compressed air, open case. | | Monitor temperatures | After heavy load | Software like HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner. | | Overclock (optional) | Once comfortable | Adjust settings in BIOS or overclocking utilities. | | Upgrade components | As needed | Swap out older GPUs, add RAM, upgrade SSD. | --- #### 8️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Quick Fixes | Symptom | Likely Cause | Remedy | |---------|---------------|--------| | No POST / beep codes | Wrong CPU seating, missing power connection | Re‑inspect CPU, ensure all pins engaged, double‑check PSU plugs. | | Random shutdowns | Under‑powered PSU, overheating | Confirm PSU wattage meets demand, improve airflow, reapply thermal paste. | | Blue screen after OS install | Faulty RAM or incompatible driver | Test RAM modules individually, update chipset drivers. | | Fan spins slowly | Incorrect voltage setting | In BIOS, set fan curve to higher RPM or disable PWM mode. | --- #### 🎉 Congratulations! Your brand‑new PC is ready for action. Whether you're gaming, editing videos, coding, or simply browsing, enjoy the satisfaction of having built something entirely from scratch. Happy computing! Feel free to ask if you'd like help choosing specific parts for a particular budget or usage scenario.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions or guidance. We can provide steps and considerations. No need to call function. Just answer with detailed guide.

We should cover planning (budget, components), buying parts, assembly process, installing OS, troubleshooting. Provide safety tips. Also mention compatibility checks like CPU socket, motherboard chipset, RAM type, GPU power supply requirements, case size, cooling solutions. Maybe give example builds at different budgets. Provide links maybe but not necessary. Let's produce thorough response.
